tasks.title: Strings
tasks.q: Write ticket_line(ticket_id, title, priority). It returns one line of text such as #101 Login page returns 500 [high]: the id after a #, the title with the whitespace around it removed, and the priority in lower case inside square brackets. Return the text; do not print it.
tasks.tests:
assert ticket_line(101, "Login page returns 500", "high") == "#101 Login page returns 500 [high]", "builds the line from the three values"
assert ticket_line(7, "  Printer jams \n", "low") == "#7 Printer jams [low]", "removes the whitespace around the title"
assert ticket_line(102, "Wi-Fi drops", "HIGH") == "#102 Wi-Fi drops [high]", "puts the priority in lower case"

tasks.title: Casting and truthiness
tasks.q: Write hours_label(hours). hours is a number, or None when nothing was logged. Return "not logged" for None, and otherwise the number followed by h, such as "2.5h". Zero is a real value: 0 gives "0h".
tasks.tests:
assert hours_label(2.5) == "2.5h", "a number becomes text that ends in h"
assert hours_label(None) == "not logged", "None means nothing was logged"
assert hours_label(0) == "0h", "zero hours is a real value, not a missing one"

tasks.title: Lists, tuples and range
tasks.q: Write add_ticket(queue, ticket). It returns a new list that holds every ticket in queue followed by ticket. The caller's list must be left as it was.
tasks.tests:
rows = [(1, 101, "Login page returns 500")]
result = add_ticket(rows, (2, 102, "Printer jams"))
assert result == [(1, 101, "Login page returns 500"), (2, 102, "Printer jams")], "returns the tickets with the new one at the end"
assert rows == [(1, 101, "Login page returns 500")], "leaves the caller's list as it was"
assert result is not rows, "returns a new list, not the same object"

tasks.title: Sets and binary types
tasks.q: Write new_reporters(today, known). Both arguments are lists of reporter names as typed, so the same person can appear with different capitals or stray spaces. Return a set of the names that are in today and not in known, each one stripped and lower-cased.
tasks.tests:
result = new_reporters(["Dana", " lee ", "SAM", "dana"], ["Lee"])
assert isinstance(result, set), "returns a set"
assert result == {"dana", "sam"}, "keeps who is new, each name once and cleaned up"
assert new_reporters(["Lee"], ["lee "]) == set(), "nobody new gives an empty set"

tasks.title: None and dictionaries
tasks.q: A ticket is a dict. Write assignee_of(ticket). It returns the value under "assignee", or "unassigned" when the key is missing or its value is None.
tasks.tests:
assert assignee_of({"id": 101, "assignee": "dana"}) == "dana", "returns the assignee when there is one"
assert assignee_of({"id": 102}) == "unassigned", "a missing key gives unassigned"
assert assignee_of({"id": 103, "assignee": None}) == "unassigned", "a key that holds None gives unassigned"

tasks.title: Numbers and datetime
tasks.q: Write hours_between(opened, closed). Both arguments are datetime values. Return the time between them in hours as a float, so 90 minutes is 1.5 and a ticket open for a day and two hours is 26.0.
tasks.tests:
from datetime import datetime
opened = datetime(2026, 10, 15, 9, 30)
assert hours_between(opened, datetime(2026, 10, 15, 11, 0)) == 1.5, "90 minutes is 1.5 hours"
assert hours_between(opened, datetime(2026, 10, 16, 11, 30)) == 26.0, "counts the whole days too"
assert type(hours_between(opened, opened)) is float, "returns a float"

tasks.title: Namespaces
tasks.q: This script stops with TypeError: 'list' object is not callable: its first line gives the name list to a list of tags, which hides the builtin. Change the script so the tags live under the name tags, the builtin list is left alone, and count ends up as 3.
tasks.starter:
list = ["printer", "hardware"]
letters = list("abc")
count = len(letters)
print(list, count)
tasks.tests:
import builtins
assert list is builtins.list, "list still names the builtin"
assert tags == ["printer", "hardware"], "the tags live under the name tags"
assert count == 3, "count is 3"
